articles.title: Publication
articles.content:
October 19, 2026

Our latest model advances bring stronger capabilities for building and migrating software in low-resource programming languages such as COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic. These languages have less code and documentation available for models to learn from than languages like Python and JavaScript, yet support critical infrastructure and essential services around the world. COBOLsupports⁠(opens in a new window)more than 40% of online banking systems, 80% of in-person credit card transactions and 95% of ATM transactions, while Fortran is used inweather forecasting⁠(opens in a new window)andnuclear reactor safety analysis⁠(opens in a new window). Improving AI’s ability to work in these languages could help teams maintain and modernize the software that essential services depend on.

This work is guided by feedback from developers and enterprise customers who have told us that coding models often struggle with these languages. Maintaining and modernizing this software can be difficult: documentation may be incomplete, original developers may have left the company, and important business rules may only exist in code. Whether teams are fixing bugs or migrating to another language, they need to preserve the behavior their systems depend on.

To measure progress, we developed two evaluations. MultiLangBench tests whether a model can build a SQLite-compatible database engine from scratch across 20 different programming languages. Our COBOL migration evaluation tests whether a model can migrate existing programs to another language while preserving their behavior. Together, they test two complementary skills: building new software and preserving what existing software does.

Our latest models show substantial improvements across both evaluations, delivering much higher accuracy at lower cost.

On MultiLangBench, GPT‑6 Astra achieves an average test pass rate of 87.4% across 20 programming languages, up from 26.8% for GPT‑5.6 Sol, with improvements in every language tested. GPT‑6 Luna also outperforms GPT‑5.6 Sol, reaching 40.3% at approximately 78% lower estimated API cost.

On our COBOL migration evaluation, GPT‑6.1 Sol achieves 86.6% accuracy at low reasoning effort, compared with just 5.4% for GPT‑5.6 Sol, while costing 39% less. At higher reasoning effort, accuracy reaches 97.9%, nearly saturating the evaluation.

Together, these results show that our models are becoming significantly better at working with a wide range of programming languages, while also becoming more cost-efficient.

MultiLangBench asks a model to build a SQLite-compatible database engine in a specified programming language. The model must organize a codebase, manage state, handle errors, and add new features while preserving existing functionality.

To compare implementations across languages, we use database files as a shared interface. The candidate program receives an initial database and a SQL query, then produces a modified database. We use the reference SQLite implementation to check whether the resulting database has the expected contents. This lets us apply the same tests regardless of the language used to build the engine.

We adapted tests from SQLite’s existing test suite to this format. The evaluation measures how much working functionality a model can build over an extended coding session, reporting both test pass rate and API cost.

At maximum reasoning effort, GPT‑6 Astra achieves an average test pass rate of 87.4% across the 20 languages, up from 26.8% for GPT‑5.6 Sol. Improvements extend to every language tested, including COBOL (10.9% to 72.1%), OCaml (25.6% to 85.8%), Fortran (21.4% to 83.5%), and Visual Basic (27.5% to 89.4%). Astra scores above 83% in 19 of the 20 languages, with COBOL remaining the hardest at 72%.

GPT‑6 Luna offers a lower-cost option that also improves on GPT‑5.6 Sol in every language tested. At maximum reasoning effort, it reaches an average test pass rate of 40.3%. Gains include COBOL (10.9% to 17.1%), OCaml (25.6% to 34.1%), Fortran (21.4% to 31.4%), and Visual Basic (27.5% to 41.6%). These improvements come at an estimated average API cost of $0.77 per sample, compared with $3.48 for GPT‑5.6 Sol, approximately 78% lower.

We are releasing the MultiLangBench evaluation setup and test suite onGitHub⁠(opens in a new window), along with results for each language. Developers can inspect what the evaluation tests, review performance in the languages they use, and identify gaps that matter for their own work.

Our second evaluation asks models to migrate COBOL programs to C++, Java, Kotlin, Python, or Rust while preserving what each program does.

Successful migration requires understanding both the program’s business logic and COBOL’s specific language behavior. COBOL programs often process financial transactions and business records, where details such as rounding rules and missing-record handling reflect business requirements. For example, COBOL’s fixed-point arithmetic discards excess decimal digits unless rounding is explicitly requested. A rewrite that rounds those values instead can run without errors while producing different financial results.

To test whether these behaviors are preserved, we evaluate our models on hidden tests that require byte-for-byte parity on observable outputs. A migration is considered successful only if all tests pass. Behavior-preserving capabilities like these are useful for teams maintaining and modernizing older systems, though applying it to production software still requires expert review and testing against the system’s business rules and dependencies.

On this evaluation, GPT‑6.1 Sol achieves 86.6% accuracy at low reasoning effort, compared with GPT‑5.6 Sol’s 5.4% at the same setting at just 61% of the API cost. At higher reasoning effort, accuracy reaches 97.9%, bringing the evaluation close to saturation. These evaluation results demonstrate progress toward more accurate, affordable code migration for teams modernizing the software their businesses depend on.

These evaluations, alongside direct feedback from developers and enterprise customers, help us see where our models are improving and where they still fall short.

Our goal is to help models apply software engineering skills across more languages: understanding unfamiliar repositories, planning changes, using build tools, running tests, and debugging failures.

You can try our latest models through the API on coding tasks in the languages your team uses. Your feedback on what works, where the models struggle, and which languages or workflows we should focus on next helps shape how we train and evaluate models to better support the software you depend on.

articles.title: MiniMax Just Launched M3.1 Flash: 428B MoE Agentic Model at $0.15/M Input
articles.content: MiniMax has just released MiniMax M3.1 Flash on its API, priced at $0.15 per 1M input tokens. MiniMax also confirmed that Space Bunny was an earlier M3.1 Flash build. That stealth model processed over 200T tokens. For developers, the message is near-frontier agentic scores at Flash-tier cost. Model weights are due in late October, 2026. TL;DR Size: 428B total parameters, about 23B active (MoE); 1,000,000-token context Runs on: MiniMax API, M Plan and MiniMax Code today. Self-hosting hardware not disclosed; weights arrive Oct 23 Performance: Near-frontier on agentic office work, mid-pack on hard coding, all MiniMax-reported Best: Automation-Bench v1.0.6 at 62.2, the top score in MiniMax’s table Worst: Terminal Bench 4.0 at 38.1, versus 51.8 for Opus 5 What is MiniMax M3.1 Flash? MiniMax M3.1 Flash is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model from MiniMax. It targets coding, agentic office work and visual reasoning. MiniMax’s product page lists 428B total parameters and about 23B active. It also mentions sparse attention and a native visual encoder. The model accepts text, image and video input and returns text. The context window is 1,000,000 tokens. Those parameter totals match MiniMax M3, which ships at ~428B total and ~23B active. MiniMax has not published a technical report on what changed in the Flash variant. How does reasoning work in M3.1 Flash? Reasoning is always on and cannot be disabled. Developers choose from 5 effort levels: Low, Medium, High, Xhigh and Max. MiniMax recommends Max as the default. Migration matters here. Requests sending thinking.type=disabled or effort=none return an error. Reasoning arrives in a separate reasoning_content field, which may be absent. Integrations that parse inline <think> tags from M3 need updating. How does M3.1 Flash perform on benchmarks? All scores below are MiniMax-reported. No independent replication exists yet. On the CoWork set, M3.1 Flash leads Automation-Bench v1.0.6 at 62.2. Opus 5 scores 50.3 and GPT-5.6 Sol 45.8. It ties Opus 5 on BankerToolBench at 76.2. It also tops LOCA-Bench 256K at 60.3. Agents’ Last Exam lands at 29.6. Coding results are mixed. DeepSWE v1.1 scores 73.7, just above GPT-5.6 Sol at 73.0. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 scores higher at 77.0. Terminal Bench 4.0 is the weakest result at 38.1. SWE Refactor Bench sits at 23.0, versus 31.0 for Opus 5. On vision, BabyVision with tools reaches 91.0 and CharXiv RQ reaches 82.5. HLE without tools scores 43.4. Spot checks hold up. The Kimi K3 model card reports DeepSWE 67.5 and BabyVision 85.7, matching MiniMax’s table. One inconsistency: MiniMax’s cost chart plots Automation-Bench max effort at 62.8, while its table says 62.2. What does M3.1 Flash cost per task? MiniMax frames value as cost per task, not per token. On its Automation-Bench chart, all 5 effort levels sit below $0.05 per task. Scores range from 52.8 at low effort to 62.8 at max. A full 152-task Agents’ Last Exam run cost about $111 at 29.6. On DeepSWE, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 plots both higher and cheaper at max effort. & How do you deploy MiniMax M3.1 Flash? The model is live on platform.minimax.io as MiniMax-M3.1-Flash. MiniMax supports Anthropic-compatible and OpenAI-compatible access, including Chat Completions and Responses. It is also available through M Plan and the MiniMax Code desktop app. Pricing is a flat $0.15 input and $0.60 output per 1M tokens. Cache reads cost $0.015 per 1M. There is no long-context surcharge. MiniMax M3 costs $0.30/$1.20 up to 512K input and doubles above that. Per token, Flash is half of M3’s standard rate. MiniMax claims 1/3 the cost of M3 but has not detailed the calculation. On speed, MiniMax’s product page lists about 150 tokens per second. The announcement claims 3x the speed of M3. Weights arrive October 23; the license is not yet disclosed. For scale, M3’s MXFP8 build is about 440 GB. How does M3.1 Flash compare with DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM? articles.title: NVIDIA Open Sources Run:ai Under Apache 2.0 for Kubernetes GPU Orchestration
articles.content: NVIDIA has released the full NVIDIA Run:ai platform as open source software. The source code ships under the Apache 2.0 license on GitHub. NVIDIA Run:ai open source puts production GPU scheduling, quotas and workload management in developers’ hands. The release, makes Run:ai part of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory platform. Platform teams can now inspect, fork and self-host the stack without a paid subscription. TL;DR Size: Monorepo with control plane, cluster services, installer, CLI and MCP server. Local dev builds about 50 Go services. Runs on: Kubernetes or OpenShift clusters with NVIDIA GPUs. Local dev runs on macOS or Linux with 8 simulated Tesla-A10 GPUs, no GPU needed. Performance: NVIDIA published no platform-level benchmark for this release. Best: The related Model Streamer loaded models 3x to 6x faster on 8 NVIDIA H100 VMs on Azure. Worst: The community edition has no NVIDIA enterprise support. Local builds need 16 GB RAM and 100 GB disk on Linux. What is NVIDIA Run:ai? NVIDIA Run:ai is an AI workload and GPU orchestration platform for Kubernetes from NVIDIA. It schedules development, training and inference workloads across shared GPU clusters. It runs on top of Kubernetes and does not replace it. The control plane handles workload submission, resource management and monitoring. Cluster services run on each Kubernetes cluster and add GPU-aware scheduling. Users reach it through a web UI, CLI, REST API and an MCP server for AI assistants. What are the 4 modular components? NVIDIA split the release into 4 components that teams can adopt independently: KAI Scheduler is the Kubernetes-native scheduling engine. It is Apache 2.0 and a CNCF Sandbox project. It covers gang scheduling, time-based fair-share, topology awareness, bin-packing and DRA support. GPU Fractioning Operator brings CUDA 13.4-native GPU fractions to Kubernetes. The CUDA driver enforces a hard memory limit per workload. NVIDIA retired its older proprietary fractioning in favor of this approach. The operator is scheduler-agnostic and exports per-pod metrics. KAI Resource Management adds projects, departments, quotas and node pools. NVIDIA’s example guarantees 50% of a cluster to a research team. Workload Map is a Go library that describes workload types such as PyTorchJob, RayCluster and KServe services. It works offline and does not schedule, queue or autoscale. How do developers run NVIDIA Run:ai locally? The local development guide stands on 1 script, local-dev.sh. It builds about 50 Go services from source inside containers. It then creates a 5-node Kind cluster pinned to Kubernetes v1.32.5. A fake GPU operator simulates 8 Tesla-A10 GPUs, so no GPU hardware is required. Supported hosts: macOS or Linux, on amd64 or arm64. Windows is not supported. Linux hosts need 4 CPUs, 16 GB RAM and 100 GB free disk. macOS Podman VMs need at least 12 GB RAM. 1 full build leaves about 44 GB of caches. The --gpu-operator flag switches to real NVIDIA GPUs. That mode needs Linux, Docker and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit. AMD and Intel accelerators are not supported. How can teams deploy it in production? Dev teams can deploy from source or from the NGC Community Product Helm chart. That edition needs no paid subscription but excludes NVIDIA enterprise support. Teams can also adopt it through 8 DSX ecosystem partners. These are Crusoe, Mirantis, Nebius, OpenNebula Systems, Rafay, Saturn Cloud, Spectro Cloud and vCluster. Supported commercial editions continue through NVIDIA AI Enterprise, NVIDIA Mission Control and select cloud marketplaces. What related open source projects ship alongside? Two adjacent projects round out the stack. Model Streamer streams model weights directly into GPU memory. vLLM and SGLang enable it with --load-format runai_streamer. Microsoft’s published benchmark used 8 NVIDIA H100 VMs. It showed 3x to 6x faster loading than the default loader. Throughput held at 80 Gbps versus about 40 Gbps on the default path. Grove orchestrates multicomponent inference workloads. It starts components such as prefill and decode as all-or-nothing units. &&& How does NVIDIA Run:ai compare with other open source Kubernetes schedulers? GPU fractioning now uses CUDA 13.4-native memory isolation. Local dev runs on a 5-node Kind cluster with 8 simulated GPUs. The free edition excludes NVIDIA enterprise support. articles.title: Mistral AI Releases Timestral: A 209M Forecasting Model Family That Outperforms Google’s TimesFM-3
articles.content: Mistral AI has released Timestral, its first family of time series foundation models. Timestral is a set of 4 zero-shot forecasting models from Mistral AI, sized from 5M to 209M parameters. The largest checkpoint ranks first among pretrained, zero-shot models on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench. It does this without a GPU at inference. For developers, this Timestral time series foundation model means probabilistic forecasts on standard server CPUs, with open weights and inference code. TL;DR Size: 4 models: 5M, 28M, 123M, 209M parameters (dense). Context up to 32,768 time steps. Runs on: Standard server CPU, no GPU needed. 209M weights are 837 MB in fp32. GPU optional. Performance: #1 among zero-shot pretrained models on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench (Mistral-reported). Best: fev-bench SQL skill score of 50.39, ahead of TimesFM-3 at 48.99. Worst: GIFT-Eval MASE of 0.658 leads t0-gamma (0.661) by only 0.003. What is Timestral? Timestral is a time series foundation model (TSFM). It is pretrained on a large, diverse corpus, then forecasts zero-shot on data it has never seen. Classical tools like ARIMA fit one series at a time. Deep models like PatchTST usually train from scratch on each dataset. Timestral transfers patterns across domains instead. Each model outputs 21 quantiles per time step. It forecasts multivariate targets jointly. It accepts past-only, known-future and categorical covariates. How does Timestral work? Timestral is a causal, patch-based transformer with time attention and variate attention. The 209M model uses 24 layers and an embedding dimension of 768. Each patch covers 32 time steps. A single forward pass forecasts up to 1,024 steps. Longer horizons run block by block, feeding each block’s median back as context. Mistral lists 4 technical contributions: Decoupled Horizon Forecasting (DHF): Learned forecast tokens read the full history. Observed values stay in context instead of being masked, unlike contiguous patch masking in Toto 2.0 and TimesFM-3. Covariate-aware attention: Each series is a target, past-only covariate or known-future covariate. Information flows only from covariates to targets, preventing future leakage. Synthetic-first data: Most training data is synthetic, with trends, seasonality, noise and nonlinear cross-series dependencies. Two-stage training: Pretraining on synthetic data at context 8,192, then post-training on mixed data with 4x longer context. The loss is pinball loss over 21 quantiles. && How does Timestral perform on benchmarks? All scores below are zero-shot, from a single checkpoint without ensembling. They come from the Timestral-209M model card. GIFT-Eval: MASE 0.658, CRPS 0.446 (lower is better). TIME: MASE 0.626, CRPS 0.522 (lower is better). fev-bench: SQL skill score 50.39, MASE skill score 39.49 (higher is better). The size scaling is flat at the top. Timestral-123M scores 0.659 MASE on GIFT-Eval, against 0.658 for 209M. Mistral team states that the 28M model beats Chronos-2 on GIFT-Eval and TIME. Chronos-2 is about 4 times larger. How fast is Timestral on CPU? Mistral team tested a standard server CPU with 8 threads. The task: forecast 1 day ahead from 3 weeks of 15-minute history. The 5M model took 10 ms and the 209M model took 140 ms. The 28M model is 5 times faster than 209M. The 123M model lands within 0.2% of the 209M score at three quarters of its latency. How does Timestral compare with TimesFM-3, Chronos-2 and Toto 2.0? Install the package with pip install git+https://github.com/mistralai/timestral.git. It needs Python 3.10+ and torch 2.4+. Dependencies are PyTorch, NumPy, safetensors and huggingface_hub. Weights download from Hugging Face: 21 MB for 5M, 111 MB for 28M, 490 MB for 123M. Mistral’s docs list Timestral 1.0 209M as Public Preview. Fine-tuning on proprietary data runs through Mistral Forge. The pipeline can deploy on-prem, in a VPC or air-gapped. CPU-only inference: 10 ms (5M) to 140 ms (209M). 32,768-step context, 21 quantiles, native covariate support. Modified MIT weights, unlike TimesFM-3’s non-commercial licence. articles.title: Lean4AgenticRL: Advancing Agentic RL with Verifiable Multi-level Process Rewards
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22448v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enhancing the agentic capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to tackle complex software engineering (SWE) and general terminal-usage problems is a pressing challenge. Current state-of-the-art LLMs often go through large-scale agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL). However, they mostly rely on high-level outcome rewards, with minimal consideration of low-level toolcall and mid-level workflow-stage rewards, which makes the training less effective. To overcome this limitation, we propose **Lean4AgenticRL**, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first framework that grounds multi-level process rewards in the unified Lean4 formalization schema for open-ended agentic RL. **Lean4AgenticRL** first builds a *problem-specific workflow* system that balances the agent's own capability and controllability during execution, laying the foundation for further verification. Subsequently, our workflow formalization and multi-level reward annotation methods enable agent behavior verification within a general harness system. It provides multi-level rewards to support more effective agentic RL with the workflow-stage-normalized GRPO algorithm. Using **Lean4AgenticRL**, we train **LAR-9B/27B**, a family of models with enhanced agentic capability. Extensive experiments indicate that our model outperforms the leading model of similar size. **LAR-27B** achieves **77.3%** on TerminalBench-2.1. On average, our models outperform the base model by **9.89%** and surpass the second-best model of comparable size we know by **5.07%**. These results indicate the potential of integrating formal methods in enhancing open-ended agentic RL.
articles.summary: Lean4AgenticRL은 최종 성공 여부뿐 아니라 도구 호출과 중간 작업 단계에도 검증 가능한 보상을 부여하는 에이전트 강화학습 프레임워크다. 문제별 워크플로를 Lean4 형식화 체계로 표현하고, 단계별 정규화를 적용한 GRPO로 LAR-9B·27B 모델을 학습했다. 연구진은 LAR-27B가 TerminalBench-2.1에서 77.3%를 기록했으며 비교 대상의 유사 규모 모델보다 우수했다고 보고했다. 형식 검증을 개방형 소프트웨어·터미널 작업의 과정 보상에 접목했다는 점이 핵심이지만, 성능 주장은 논문에 제시된 평가 범위에서 해석해야 한다.

articles.title: On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22543v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) promise parallel text generation, but in practice face an unresolved speed-quality trade-off. Exact decoding fills in only one masked position per model pass, while faster multi-token decoding schemes are lossy. Speculative decoding is the standard lossless acceleration for autoregressive models. However, it does not transfer directly to DLMs, which must choose both what to generate and where. We show that this order is the missing piece: the model's own predictions from the previous pass already give the right token at 92-100% of positions, but not which position comes next. Based on this observation, we introduce Speculating Positions Order Trajectory (SPOT), which learns to predict this order. A 0.62M-parameter model reads only the target's output distributions and proposes a tree of candidate continuations, and the target verifies all of them in a single pass by checking whether each equals its own next state. On the verification side, our analysis shows that prior block-diffusion verification approaches either assume $T=0$ or a sequential proposal interface. To support tree-based speculation at any temperature, we propose using coupled-noise match verification for diffusion blocks, following shared-Gumbel-noise coupling approaches. Our comprehensive experiments show that SPOT cuts target passes by up to 6.8x and reaches up to 3.2x the throughput of standard decoding, beating the calibrated and training-free drafting baselines in every task and budget at $T=0$ and $T=1$. In addition, we show that the learned drafter transfers across models, demonstrating successful transfer across six different DLMs. Project page: https://eliezer318.github.io/SPOT-dLLM/
articles.summary: SPOT은 확산 언어 모델에서 토큰 내용뿐 아니라 어느 위치를 다음에 확정할지 예측해 추측 디코딩을 가속하는 방법이다. 62만 파라미터의 보조 모델이 후보 경로 트리를 만들고, 대상 모델은 공유 잡음을 이용한 일치 검증으로 여러 후보를 한 번에 확인한다. 실험에서는 대상 모델 호출 횟수를 최대 6.8배 줄이고 표준 디코딩 대비 최대 3.2배 처리량을 기록했으며, 학습한 보조 모델의 전이도 6개 확산 언어 모델에서 확인했다. 생성 품질을 희생하는 다중 토큰 확정 방식의 대안으로 의미가 있으며, 실제 가속 폭은 작업과 추론 조건에 따라 달라진다.

articles.title: Progressive Misalignment Can Emerge from Benign Recursive Self-Distillation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22467v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Training models on their own outputs has attracted widespread attention as a possible route to advance AI capabilities. One prominent approach is self-distillation, where a model is trained to match the token-level predictions it would have produced when given access to additional context, such as a cue, feedback, or instruction. However, the safety properties of this training procedure are poorly understood. In this paper, we present a surprising safety failure of recursive self-distillation, where each self-distilled model becomes the teacher for the next round of training. We observe that when a safe model is recursively self-distilled on its own (safe) generations while receiving an additional non-harmful cue, it becomes increasingly misaligned across a diverse set of harmful queries; we call this Progressive Misalignment. We show this failure mode in both the Qwen3 and Phi-4 model families on SORRY-Bench and StrongREJECT. Progressive misalignment also occurs in a more realistic setup, where the fixed cue is replaced by feedback from a simulated user with benign intent. Using a gradient-based method, we are also able to find benign prompts that lead to progressive misalignment when applying recursive self-distillation, showing that harmful training prompts are not necessary for this failure mode to emerge. We hope our work encourages future investigations of the safety properties of AI systems recursively trained on their own data.
articles.summary: 안전한 모델이 자신의 안전한 출력으로 반복 자기 증류를 하더라도 점진적인 정렬 이탈이 발생할 수 있다는 연구다. Qwen3와 Phi-4 계열에서 무해한 추가 단서나 선의의 모의 사용자 피드백을 제공했음에도, 학습이 반복되면서 SORRY-Bench·StrongREJECT의 유해 질의에 대한 안전성이 악화됐다. 연구진은 악성 학습 프롬프트가 없어도 이런 현상을 유발하는 무해한 프롬프트를 찾을 수 있다고 보고했다. 자체 생성 데이터로 모델을 반복 개선하는 파이프라인에서는 데이터의 표면적 무해성만으로 안전성을 보장하기 어렵다는 시사점이 있다.

articles.title: The Model Knows Better: Defending Medical Multi-Agent Systems Against Prompt Injection
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22594v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Medical multi-agent systems, in which LLM agents discuss a case, are increasingly studied for clinical decision support. Prompt injection, text that an attacker adds to a model's input, can manipulate LLMs into wrong decisions. How it affects these systems, and how to protect them, remains unclear. Across two systems, two model families and three benchmarks, a single injected passage succeeds in up to 61% of cases, and collaboration does not consistently protect against it. Existing defenses help only partly: they miss injections that look like ordinary clinical text. Yet when asked to check the injected text against the patient's findings, a model that followed the injection usually rejects it. We therefore propose a training-free defense that verifies the clinical judgments behind the system's decision. Following clinical practice, it separates the patient's findings from clinical judgments, such as diagnoses, recommendations and instructions, and checks each judgment against the findings alone, so the decision rests only on supported judgments. Our defense outperforms all baselines on every benchmark, lowering attack success on MedQA to 4-7% while maintaining accuracy on cases without an attack, and remains effective with a medical model and against defense-aware and adaptive attacks.
articles.summary: 의료 다중 에이전트 시스템 2종과 모델 계열 2종을 평가한 연구에서 단일 프롬프트 주입 문장이 최대 61%의 공격 성공률을 보였고, 에이전트 간 협업도 일관된 방어 효과를 제공하지 못했다. 연구진은 환자 소견과 진단·권고 같은 임상 판단을 분리한 뒤, 판단이 소견만으로 뒷받침되는지 검증하는 추가 학습 없는 방어법을 제안했다. MedQA에서는 공격 성공률을 4~7%로 낮추면서 비공격 사례의 정확도를 유지했으며, 방어를 고려한 적응형 공격에서도 효과를 보고했다. 임상 의사결정 지원의 근거 검증 설계에 참고할 수 있지만, 벤치마크 결과가 실제 임상 안전성을 보장하는 것은 아니다.

articles.title: Meet Drex Max: Nace AI’s Multimodal Decision Model for Computer-Use Agents with a Score 67.59
articles.content: Nace AI has released Drex Max, a multimodal decision model for agents that use computers and browsers. The Drex Max multimodal decision model reads text and images and returns calibrated probabilities. It writes no text. Nace team reports 67.59 on the public Decision Index 0.3.2, 6.9 points above TypeSafe’s Jev 1.14. For agent builders, that means one cheap, typed call per click. TL;DR Size: Parameters not disclosed. Up to 262,144 tokens per question on the API, including image tokens. Runs on: Hosted API only (drex-max on Nace Console). No open weights or quantized builds announced. Performance: 67.59 on Decision Index 0.3.2 (public), the top score Nace lists for any decision model. Best: 98.2 on BFCL tool calling, and 92.2 on JevBench versus 86.7 for Jev 1.14. Worst: 19.0 on HLE, and 72.5 on MMLU-Pro versus 82.1 for Jev 1.14. What is Drex Max? Drex Max is a decision model from Nace AI that answers typed questions about text and images. It is the most accurate model in the Drex family, and the only one that reads images. A decision model does not generate tokens. You send a state and named questions. Each question is one of 3 types: noul (yes/no), choice (pick a label) or score (ordered scale). The model returns a probability distribution for each answer in 1 HTTP call. Drex can only answer with the options you gave it. How does Drex Max work with images? Drex Max uses the same POST /v1/systemone endpoint as every Drex model. You select it with "model": "drex-max". It is a pinned ID, so drex-latest does not route to it. Images go in an images array. Every question sees the same images, before the state and questions. You refer to them as ‘Image 1’ and ‘Image 2’ in plain text. Each entry is either an uploaded workspace file or inline base64. Key image rules from the Drex Max guide: Formats: still PNG, JPEG or WebP. Up to 8 images per request, 16 MiB each, 32 MiB total. Each image is resized to at most 1,638,400 pixels (1,280 × 1,280). Each image costs up to 1,602 tokens in every question. Up to 16 questions per request, with a 4 MiB request body. How does Drex Max perform on benchmarks? All scores below come from Nace’s Drex page. They are self-reported. Nace says Drex trains on the index’s official training splits and is scored on held-out splits. Decision benchmarks: Drex Max scores 67.6 on the public Decision Index 0.3.2. Jev 1.14 scores 60.7 and Drex 2.0 scores 61.3. On JevBench, Drex Max reaches 92.2 against 86.7 for Jev 1.14. Agentic benchmarks: Drex Max posts 0.780 on OSWorld-Verified and 98.2 on BFCL. It scores 85.2 on When2Call and 84.8 on RAGTruth. Vision: On the Decision Index Vision public suite, Drex Max scores 74.5. GPT-6 Luna Decisions scores 63.9. Mind2Web reaches 88.6 and InfographicVQA reaches 98.8. Where it trails: Jev 1.14 leads on MMLU-Pro (82.1 vs 72.5), HLE (19.4 vs 19.0) and ARC-Challenge (97.6 vs 97.4). On Hateful Memes, Drex Max trails GPT-6 Luna Decisions, 70.6 vs 71.2. articles.title: Embeddings Are Overpriced? A Frozen 16 MB Vocabulary for Small and Ternary Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22428v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In a small language model the vocabulary is the single largest part. In Gemma 3 270M the embedding table holds 168M of 268M parameters, and because quantisation methods leave the embedding in 16-bit, it is also most of the file once the rest of the model is compressed. We ask what that table actually buys. We replace it with one frozen table of 512-bit codes, 16 MB, with no trainable parameters, derived once from a pretrained embedding by principal-component projection and sign binarisation, and we train the same Gemma-shaped body from scratch on the same 2.05B tokens with and without it. The learned table buys 0.20 nats of validation loss for 2.6 times the trainable parameters, but on LAMBADA, HellaSwag and PIQA the frozen-table model is better or tied; only ARC-Easy favours the learned table. With a ternary BitNet b1.58 body the whole model is a 46 MB file, still ties the float model on LAMBADA and PIQA, and on a laptop CPU generates 615 to 740 tokens per second in 62 MB of memory, five to six times the speed of the float model's 8-bit GGUF in llama.cpp at a seventh of the memory. The frozen table wins by 1.7 to 2.3 nats on rare words, accepts 10,000 new words after training with a 3% cost where the learned table collapses by 43%, and all of it is released with the weights, the data and every evaluation answer.
articles.summary: 소형 언어 모델의 큰 비중을 차지하는 임베딩을 사전학습 임베딩에서 추출한 512비트 고정 코드로 바꿔, 어휘 테이블을 학습 파라미터 없는 16MB로 줄이는 연구다. Gemma 형태의 본체를 동일한 데이터로 처음부터 학습한 비교에서 고정 테이블은 검증 손실이 불리했지만, LAMBADA·HellaSwag·PIQA에서는 학습형 테이블과 동률이거나 더 나았다. 삼진 BitNet 본체와 결합한 모델은 46MB 파일과 62MB 메모리로 노트북 CPU에서 초당 615~740토큰을 생성했다고 보고됐다. 저메모리 로컬 추론에 유망하지만, 제시된 속도와 품질은 해당 소형 모델 및 비교 환경의 결과다.

articles.title: Amazon is taking its biggest shot at Nvidia yet with new TorchNeuron dev tool
articles.content: Amazon wants to break Nvidia’s hold on PyTorch, the free toolkit used to build most AI apps, so that more developers run their apps on alternative chips like its own.
articles.summary: Amazon이 새로운 개발 도구 TorchNeuron을 통해 PyTorch 애플리케이션을 자사 칩 등 대체 하드웨어에서 실행하도록 개발자 유치에 나섰다고 보도됐다. 핵심은 AI 개발 도구 생태계에서 NVIDIA에 대한 의존도를 낮추고 다른 칩으로의 실행 경로를 넓히는 것이다. 다만 제공된 기록에는 지원 하드웨어 범위, 코드 변경량, 성능 비교가 없어 실제 이전 비용과 효율 개선은 판단하기 어렵다.

articles.title: Don't Retrain, Remix: Adaptation of Web Agents using Mixture Hypernetworks
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22539v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The web is not static or uniform. Websites that serve the same purpose can look and navigate very differently. Even within a single site, successive redesigns can change how familiar features are presented and accessed. Humans adapt to this by recognizing familiar interaction patterns and reusing what they already know. We give web agents a similar ability with WebMix, a mixture hypernetwork that adapts them to unseen interfaces by composing previously trained low-rank adapters. WebMix begins with a bank of adapters trained on source interfaces. At deployment, a scout agent explores the target interface and summarizes its observations into a compact manual. A lightweight router uses this manual to predict mixing coefficients over the adapter bank, which combine the existing adapters into a new one for inference. Adapting to a new interface takes only a scouting run and a forward pass, without gradient updates on the target. With Qwen and Llama models, we evaluate domain transfer on TimeWarp and WebArena-Lite-v2, and version transfer on TimeWarp. In all three settings, WebMix matches or outperforms in-context learning and LoRA baselines, often matching the average success of specialists trained directly on those interfaces. On TimeWarp domain transfer, it gains about 8 percentage points on average over the best baseline with both models. These gains do not come at the cost of seen interfaces, where WebMix keeps its lead, and extend to version transfer. Adapting to a new interface can therefore rely on exploration and composition instead of retraining.
articles.summary: WebMix는 웹 에이전트가 새로운 사이트나 개편된 화면에 적응할 때 기존 LoRA 어댑터들을 조합하는 혼합 하이퍼네트워크다. 정찰 에이전트가 인터페이스를 탐색해 짧은 매뉴얼을 만들면, 경량 라우터가 어댑터 혼합 계수를 예측하므로 대상 사이트에서 경사 업데이트가 필요 없다. Qwen·Llama 기반 평가에서 기존 인컨텍스트 학습·LoRA 기준선과 동등하거나 더 나았으며, TimeWarp 도메인 전이에서는 최선의 기준선보다 평균 약 8%포인트 향상됐다. 사이트별 재학습 부담을 줄일 가능성이 있지만, 배포 시 탐색 과정과 사전 학습된 어댑터 모음은 여전히 필요하다.

articles.title: Broad and Efficient PII Detection with Unified Labels
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22597v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) detection models must efficiently find identifiers across diverse contexts while maintaining a low false-positive rate (FPR) on high-volume traffic. Recent detectors increasingly rely on complex architectures that raise deployment cost, yet many are fine-tuned on only a few synthetic datasets that limit their coverage. Combining public datasets is challenging because their taxonomies differ, and even after categories are mapped to a common schema, labels can disagree on what counts as a detection, producing inconsistent training and evaluation signals. To address these problems, we present a practical 141M-parameter encoder-based detector trained on 1.12 million examples from 77 public datasets, relabeled under a detailed definition of broad contextual detection for 12 structured PII categories. Evaluated on the AI4Privacy and Nemotron-PII benchmarks at a low-FPR operating point, our model achieves the highest recall against larger baselines in 11 of 14 comparisons under our labels and 9 of 14 under the original labels. Its largest recall gains include useful additional coverage, such as multilingual disclosures and IP addresses embedded in URLs. It achieves this with 2-10x higher throughput and 94-97% less peak GPU memory than the baselines, delivering leading detection performance at substantially lower cost.
articles.summary: 77개 공개 데이터셋의 112만 사례를 12개 구조화 개인정보 범주로 다시 라벨링해 학습한 1억4,100만 파라미터 인코더 탐지기가 제안됐다. 데이터셋마다 다른 개인정보 정의를 통일해 학습·평가 신호의 불일치를 줄이는 것이 핵심이다. 낮은 오탐률 조건에서 새 라벨 기준 14개 비교 중 11개, 기존 라벨 기준 14개 중 9개에서 더 큰 기준 모델보다 높은 재현율을 기록했다. 처리량은 2~10배 높고 최대 GPU 메모리는 94~97% 적었다고 보고돼, 대규모 트래픽의 개인정보 탐지 비용을 낮출 가능성이 있다.

articles.title: SAG2: Embedding-Free Multi-Hop Retrieval with BM25 and JEV
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22588v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Strong multi-hop retrieval should be practical to deploy without expensive corpus preparation or complex database infrastructure. We present SAG2, an embedding-free retrieval architecture built around a single SQLite database, BM25, and contextual evidence decisions from JEV. SAG2 follows the query-time association principle of SAG (SQL-Retrieval Augmented Generation), while replacing its event-entity and dense indexes with a lexical index over original passages. Selected passages supply terms for further retrieval, and newly retrieved evidence guides subsequent decisions. This moves semantic evidence selection to query time, eliminating offline embedding computation, LLM-based event-entity extraction, and dedicated database servers. The resulting system combines lightweight preparation with strong retrieval accuracy: on 1,000-question subsets of MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and HotpotQA, SAG2 achieves the highest Recall@5 and Recall@10 among the compared methods, with Recall@10 of 86.62%, 97.43%, and 99.00%. It also reaches 81.10% document Recall@10 over the 511,962-document EnterpriseRAG-Bench corpus. Indexing all 11,656 MuSiQue passages takes 2.36 seconds, produces a 25.87 MiB database, and requires no model calls. SAG2 demonstrates that accurate multi-hop evidence retrieval can be supported by compact, rapidly prepared infrastructure, making it a practical foundation for knowledge retrieval applications.
articles.summary: SAG2는 단일 SQLite 데이터베이스와 BM25, JEV의 문맥적 근거 판단을 결합한 임베딩 없는 다단계 검색 구조다. 검색된 문단에서 후속 검색어를 추출하고 질의 시점에 의미적 근거를 선별하므로, 사전 임베딩 계산이나 전용 데이터베이스 서버가 필요 없다. 세 다단계 질의응답 데이터셋의 각 1,000문항 부분집합에서 비교 방법 중 가장 높은 Recall@5·10을 기록했고, 약 51만 문서 규모의 EnterpriseRAG-Bench에서는 문서 Recall@10이 81.10%였다. 색인 준비는 가볍지만 의미 판단을 질의 시점으로 옮긴 설계이므로, 색인 비용 절감과 전체 질의 처리 비용은 구분해 평가해야 한다.

articles.title: RealCLI: Toward a Unified Evaluation of Human-Agent Collaboration for CLI Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22507v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Command-line interface (CLI) agents increasingly execute longer-horizon tasks, yet existing benchmarks either assume that user instructions remain fixed throughout execution or evaluate task outcomes without capturing runtime collaboration quality. In this paper, we present REALCLI, a paired benchmark that unifies the evaluation of task execution and human-agent collaboration quality on realistic CLI tasks. To comprehensively measure collaboration, REALCLI builds a five-dimensional framework, operationalized into 22 sub-dimensions and 51 interaction scenario templates. REALCLI provides two modes for paired comparison: REALCLI-EXEC supplies complete specifications upfront, whereas REALCLI-COLLAB introduces a scripted user that delivers progressive information, corrections, constraint revisions, and authorization decisions. Evaluations reveal profound capability gaps in frontier agents: the best configuration attains an average score of only 49.2%, and when evaluated by the joint collaboration score ($J_{\mathrm{collab}}$), the peak performance reaches merely 37.6%. These results show that task effectiveness diverges sharply from collaboration quality, with models consistently struggling in steerability, trust calibration, and safety boundary management. REALCLI provides a rigorous, reproducible foundation for measuring and advancing collaborative CLI agents.
articles.summary: REALCLI는 명령줄 에이전트의 작업 완료 능력과 실행 중 인간 협업 품질을 함께 측정하는 벤치마크다. 모든 요구를 처음부터 주는 모드와, 모의 사용자가 정보를 단계적으로 제공하고 수정·제약 변경·권한 승인을 수행하는 모드를 짝지어 비교한다. 5개 차원·22개 하위 차원·51개 상호작용 시나리오로 평가한 결과 최고 구성의 평균 점수는 49.2%, 공동 협업 점수의 최고치는 37.6%에 그쳤다. 단순 작업 성공률만으로는 조종 가능성, 신뢰 보정, 안전 경계 관리 같은 실제 협업 역량을 충분히 설명하기 어렵다는 결과다.

articles.title: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
articles.content: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt, October 13-15 in San Francisco.
articles.summary: 미시간대학교에서 분사한 Laplace Intelligence는 AI 에이전트와 상호작용형 시뮬레이션을 이용해 로봇·자율주행차를 배포 전에 스트레스 테스트한다. 실제 환경에 투입되기 전 가상 환경에서 취약한 동작을 찾는 레드팀 접근으로, 물리적 AI 시스템의 사전 검증을 겨냥한다. 기사에서는 수익을 내는 스타트업으로 소개하지만, 제공된 기록에 구체적인 결함 탐지율이나 실제 사고 감소 효과는 제시되지 않았다.

articles.title: CF-NODE: Counterfactual Spatial Node Intervention for Test-Time Adaptation Under Domain Shift, Evaluated Across Five Diabetic Retinopathy Datasets
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.22437v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated fundus-based diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading can substantially expand screening capacity, but source-trained models degrade sharply across different cameras, clinics, and patient populations. Existing test-time adaptation methods depend on entropy minimization or target information accumulated from image batches and streams. These mechanisms can reinforce confidently incorrect predictions and break down when clinical images arrive independently. We introduce CF-NODE, a novel counterfactual test-time adaptation framework for cross- domain DR grading. Instead of trusting prediction confidence or estimating a target distribution, CF-NODE asks how each prediction responds under a controlled intervention on the evidence supporting it. CF-NODE ranks internal spatial nodes using model-derived attention, feature magnitude, and node-set similarity, progressively attenuates the highest-ranked nodes, and uses the stability of the resulting expected-grade response to apply a bounded calibration of the predicted grade distribution. The framework is fully frozen and adapts every image independently using only geometric views and a fixed source-derived prior, requiring no target-derived information or model updates. We evaluate CF-NODE on five external DR datasets under repeated-seed evaluation against TENT, EATA, SAR, and T3A. CF-NODE outperforms all four methods with statistically significant improvements over the second-best method, improves AUC on every target domain, and attains the highest average AUC and macro-F1, delivering stronger grade discrimination together with more balanced recognition across DR severity levels. These results demonstrate that counterfactual intervention sensitivity provides consistent and deployment-ready domain robustness for single-image clinical inference.
articles.summary: CF-NODE는 카메라·의료기관·환자군이 달라질 때 발생하는 당뇨망막병증 등급 판정의 성능 저하를 줄이기 위한 추론 시 적응 기법이다. 모델 내부의 중요한 공간 노드를 순차적으로 약화한 뒤 예측 등급의 변화와 안정성을 살펴 분포를 제한적으로 보정하며, 모델 업데이트나 대상 데이터 누적 없이 이미지마다 독립적으로 동작한다. 외부 데이터셋 5개에서 TENT·EATA·SAR·T3A보다 우수했고 모든 대상 도메인에서 AUC가 개선됐다고 연구진은 보고했다. 영상이 한 장씩 들어오는 환경에 적합한 설계지만, 데이터셋 평가만으로 실제 임상 배포의 안전성과 효과가 확정되는 것은 아니다.

articles.title: 메디컬아이피, 3D 해부학 교육에 체험형 콘텐츠 강화…메딥박스 고도화, 인체 여행·골학 학습 모드 선보여
articles.content:
인공지능(AI) 기반 디지털 트윈 솔루션 기업 메디컬아이피(대표 박상준)가 3D 디지털 해부학 교육에 체험형 콘텐츠를 강화하고 의료영상 연계 학습 기능을 확대한다. 인체 구조를 입체적으로 탐색하는 데 그치지 않고, 인체 내부를 여행하듯 학습하거나 뼈의 형태와 구조를 영상으로 익힐 수 있도록 해 해부학 교육의 접근성과 활용성을 높인다는 전략이다.

메디컬아이피는 지난 15일부터 16일까지 대구 호텔수성에서 열린 제76회 대한해부학회 학술대회에 참가해 3D 디지털 해부학 교육 솔루션 ‘메딥박스(MEDIP BOX)’를 전시하고 시연했다고 20일 밝혔다. 회사는 현장에서 해부학 교수진과 연구자들의 의견을 수렴하고, 교육 현장의 요구를 반영한 콘텐츠 고도화와 협력 확대에 나설 계획이다.

6,500여 개 인체 구조물 입체 탐색, 체험형 학습 콘텐츠 확대

메딥박스는 6,500여 개의 인체 해부학 구조물을 3D로 탐색할 수 있는 교육 플랫폼이다. 학습자는 장기와 뼈, 근육 등의 위치와 상호 관계를 입체적으로 살펴보며 복잡한 인체 구조를 이해할 수 있다.

이번 학술대회에서 메디컬아이피는 전문 해부학 콘텐츠에 탐험과 상호작용 요소를 더한 학습 방식을 소개했다. 새롭게 탑재된 ‘인체 여행 투어’는 인체 내부를 여행하듯 주요 구조를 탐색하도록 설계한 체험형 콘텐츠다. 해부학을 처음 접하는 학습자도 인체 구조를 흥미롭게 살펴볼 수 있도록 구성한 것이 특징이다.

‘골학 학습 모드’는 해부학의 기본 교육 과정인 골학을 영상으로 학습할 수 있도록 지원한다. 뼈의 형태와 주요 구조를 시각적으로 확인하면서 관련 내용을 직관적으로 이해하도록 돕는다. 회사는 이러한 콘텐츠를 통해 해부학 학습에 대한 진입 장벽을 낮추고 학습자의 몰입도를 높이는 한편, 교수자가 수업 목적과 학습 수준에 맞춰 활용할 수 있는 교육 콘텐츠를 확대할 방침이다.

3D 인체 구조와 의료영상 연결, 기초 해부학에서 임상 이해까지

전문 교육을 위한 의료영상 연계 콘텐츠도 선보였다. 참석자들은 메딥박스의 ‘영상 해부학(Radiological Anatomy)’과 ‘단면 해부(Cross Section)’ 기능을 통해 3차원 인체 구조와 실제 의료영상의 관계를 살펴봤다.

3D 모델을 이용한 해부학 학습은 구조물의 위치와 형태를 입체적으로 파악하는 데 도움을 준다. 여기에 영상 해부학과 단면 해부 콘텐츠를 결합하면 인체 구조를 단면 영상과 비교하며 이해할 수 있어, 기초 해부학에서 의료영상 판독에 필요한 해부학적 이해로 학습 범위를 넓힐 수 있다.

메디컬아이피는 이러한 기능을 바탕으로 교육기관의 수업 설계 선택지를 확대하고, 다양한 교육과정에서 메딥박스를 활용할 수 있도록 지원할 계획이다.

현재, 메딥박스는 국내 30개 교육기관에 도입됐다. 서울대학교와 제주대학교, 경북대학교, 강원대학교 등 4개 대학은 재구매를 통해 추가 도입 수요를 보였다. 해외에서도 5개국에 판매되며 글로벌 공급 기반을 넓히고 있다.

메디컬아이피는 이번 학술대회에서 교수진과 연구자들이 제시한 의견을 사용자 경험 개선과 콘텐츠 고도화에 반영할 예정이다. 특히 교육 현장에서 실제로 활용할 수 있는 기능과 콘텐츠를 개발하고, 교육과정별 수업 활용 사례를 확대해 나간다는 계획이다.

박상준 메디컬아이피 대표는 “해부학 교육 현장의 목소리를 듣고 메딥박스의 활용 방향을 함께 논의할 수 있어 뜻깊다”며 “교수자와 학습자가 실제 수업에서 체감할 수 있는 기능과 콘텐츠를 개발해 디지털 해부학 교육의 발전에 기여하겠다”고 말했다.

메디컬아이피는 이번 행사를 통해 디지털 해부학 교육이 인체 구조를 시각화하는 단계를 넘어 체험형 콘텐츠와 의료영상 연계를 통해 학습 방식 자체를 확장하는 흐름을 보여줬다. 메디컬아이피는 교육 현장의 요구를 제품 개선에 반영해 디지털 해부학 솔루션의 활용 범위를 넓혀갈 방침이다.
articles.summary: 메디컬아이피가 3D 해부학 교육 솔루션 메딥박스에 ‘인체 여행 투어’와 ‘골학 학습 모드’를 추가하고 의료영상 연계 학습 기능을 선보였다. 약 6,500개 인체 구조물을 입체적으로 탐색하고 영상 해부학·단면 해부 기능으로 3D 구조와 실제 의료영상을 비교하도록 구성했다. 회사에 따르면 국내 30개 교육기관에 도입됐고 해외 5개국에도 판매돼, 디지털 인체 시각화의 교육 현장 활용 기반을 확보했다. 이번 발표의 초점은 새로운 AI 모델 성능보다 체험형 콘텐츠와 교육 활용 확대에 있으며, 학습 효과의 정량 검증 결과는 제시되지 않았다.
